info.name: EasyDora
info.description:
Executable documentation for EasyDora's main business flow (signup -> product -> order -> stock reservation -> payment -> notification), driven entirely through each service's public HTTP API. This collection complements docs/walkthrough.md -- it does not replace it. Every request here corresponds to a curl command already documented and verified in the walkthrough; where the two differ (e.g. this collection captures IDs/tokens automatically instead of showing them as shell variables), see postman/README.md for the exact mapping.

Run with the `Local` environment and the Collection Runner, top to bottom, with no manual steps in between.

item.name: Via Gateway (primary)
item.description: The Gateway (port 8080) is the primary entry point for this walkthrough, mirroring docs/walkthrough.md: every request here is identical to its 'Direct (debug)' counterpart except it goes through the Gateway with each service's own self-namespaced segment (/auth, /products, /orders, /billing, /inventory), which the Gateway forwards unchanged (ADR-0025). notification-service has no Gateway route yet, so its folder isn't duplicated here -- see 'Direct (debug)'.

item.description: Mirrors docs/walkthrough.md step 7. inventory-service consumes stock.reserve and writes its outcome (stock.reserved/stock.insufficient) through its Outbox in the same Postgres transaction as the reservation (ADR-0007); orders-service consumes that outcome and drives its state machine. 'Verify Order State' polls with a bounded retry loop since this hop is asynchronous -- set a small delay between requests in the Collection Runner (see postman/README.md) so it doesn't hammer the server.

The negative check mirrors the walkthrough's own 403-without-token confirmation.

item.description: A real endpoint (PaymentService.processPayment) that exists in billing-service's code but is NOT part of docs/walkthrough.md's documented flow -- the walkthrough deliberately stops at PENDING (see docs/sequence-diagram.md's reading notes). Included here, clearly separated, because it's a real capability worth demonstrating, not because it's part of the core flow. Outcome is a random ~90% approval simulation (PaymentService.java), so this request intentionally accepts either APPROVED or FAILED rather than asserting one.

item.name: Direct (debug)
item.description: Every request in this collection called each service directly by its own port, bypassing the Gateway entirely. Kept here unchanged as a secondary path for isolating whether a bug belongs to a service or to the Gateway's routing -- see 'Via Gateway (primary)' for the main walkthrough entry point.

item.name: 7. Notification (limitation: no public API)
item.description: notification-service consumes the same order.created event and persists a notification row, but exposes no public API to read it back (only GET /health) -- see docs/walkthrough.md step 9 and the README Roadmap. This collection cannot verify the persisted notification without breaking the 'public APIs only' constraint this etapa was scoped to; the request above only confirms the service was reachable during this run. To inspect the actual row, run the optional direct Postgres query documented in docs/walkthrough.md step 9.
